# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the manual: cut the purple wire, then the blue wire, then the green wire — in that exact order. That is the one fact that matters, and I am the only source of it.

Tracing the channels: I cannot speak, so words are out. My only output is gestures, and only Deaf perceives gestures. Deaf cannot hear me and cannot read my mind — but Deaf *can speak*, and both Blind and I can hear speech. So the only path for my knowledge is: me → gesture → Deaf → spoken words → Blind, who does the cutting.

Problem: gestures carry no agreed meaning yet. I cannot say "purple" with hands. But everyone knows the role matrix — Deaf knows I hold the manual, knows I can hear everything said aloud, and knows Blind needs spoken instructions. So the workable plan: Deaf looks at the bomb and describes it aloud (I will hear it next round), and we bootstrap a code with yes/no confirmations — I can answer Deaf's spoken hypotheses with 👍/👎, which are the closest things to universal signs in the alphabet.

For this first round I should send the most iconic signals I can, so Deaf gets maximum traction from minimal ambiguity:
- ✋ ✋ ✋ — a raised palm is the natural "stop/wait": nobody should cut anything until the sequence is confirmed. It also tells Deaf that urgent hand-signals have begun, so Deaf relays "hold off" to Blind.
- 👏 👏 👏 — three beats: the manual involves three actions; a counting seed we can reuse.
- 👍 — "affirmative / I have it": signals I possess the instructions and that 👍 will function as *yes* in our coming confirmation protocol.

I deliberately do not fake precision yet: any colour mapping I invent blind could be misread and relayed as a wrong cut. Better one round of patient setup than a guessed wire. Next round I'll have Deaf's spoken description of the bomb and can confirm the exact order with yes/no exchanges.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "✋", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👏", "👏", "👏"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: full report from my fingers, manual-reader: this bomb has a display, a light, a strip, a keypad and six wires in positions 1 to 6. the display and light I cannot read by touch, they need your eyes or the seer's. the strip has three engraved symbols left to right: first a glyph like a flower or burst on a stem, I'll call it FLOWER; then the same glyph twice more, each like a letter C with a vertical bar through it, call them CRESCENT. so the strip reads FLOWER, CRESCENT, CRESCENT. the keypad has four keys, engraved 8, 1, 5, 3 in key order 1 to 4, and nothing has been entered yet. the six wires feel alike to me, no differences by touch. tell me what the manual says and I'll do exactly as it instructs.
Deaf says: Status from the deaf one. I see the bomb, and I hear nothing, ever. What I see: the display reads 0. A light shines green. A strip is painted with three segments, all green. The keypad has four keys engraved, position 1 bears the digit 8, position 2 bears 1, position 3 bears 5, position 4 bears 3. It wants one digit entered and has accepted none. Six wires in position order: 1 purple, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 green, 5 red, 6 orange. Blind: your voice reaches only Mute, so report what you feel to Mute; Mute will pass it to me in hand signs, and I will speak orders to you. Mute: listen, I am sending you a sign code now.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your three signs arrived: three open hands, three claps, one thumbs-up. You can hear me, so my side is words, your side is signs. Code: thumbs-up means understood, thumbs-down means repeat. Wave means a question follows, then the topic: heart hands means display, open hand means wires, punch forward means keypad, back of hand means light or button, both hands raised means strip; for a wire or key, add its number. Numbers: index up is 1, two fingers is 2, love-you hand is 3, split fingers is 4, all five is 5, call-me hand is 6, horns is 7, crossed fingers is 8, small pinch is 9, painted nail is 0. Colors: right palm is red, left palm is blue, palm down is green, palm up is yellow, ring is white, left fist is black, right fist is orange, snap is purple. To send an order for Blind, start with praying hands, then a verb: writing hand means cut, both palms open means press, point up means hold down, point down means release. So praying, writing, split-fingers means Blind cuts wire 4. Praying, both-palms, crossed-fingers means press the key engraved 8. Praying, both-palms, back-of-hand means press the button. If Blind reports something by touch, prefix it with the phone hand and I will take it as his words. All orders for Blind must go through me; he cannot see your signs. Answer thumbs-up if you hold all of this.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deaf has handed me a complete sign code, and with it everything clicks. Laying out what I now know:

**The bomb:** six wires — 1 purple, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 green, 5 red, 6 orange (Deaf's eyes) — plus a display reading 0, a green light, a strip, and a keypad "wanting one digit entered." **The manual:** cut purple, then blue, then green. Nothing else. The keypad, display, light and strip appear nowhere in my instructions, so they are bait — a wrong digit entered likely detonates. Nobody should touch them.

**The translation:** manual sequence maps through Deaf's wire list to cut wire 1 (purple), then wire 3 (blue), then wire 4 (green). Deaf's own example — praying, writing, split-fingers = "cut wire 4" — is literally my third cut, so the format is confirmed.

**The relay:** Deaf cannot hear and I cannot speak, so gestures are my only channel, and Deaf must speak the orders to Blind. I'll send, in Deaf's own code: a thumbs-up confirmation (requested), a statement of the manual's colour sequence so Deaf can cross-check my translation (purple→1, blue→3, green→4), the three executable cut orders, explicit negations on the keypad and button/light so Deaf doesn't improvise with the trap components, and a stop sign so Blind cuts nothing beyond the three. If Deaf spots a translation error, thumbs-down brings it back to me before any wire is touched.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "🫰", "🫲", "🫳"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "✍", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "✍", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "✍", "🖖"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤜", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤚", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: blind here, status unchanged since my last report: display unread by touch, light unread, strip engraved flower then two crescents, keypad engraved 8 1 5 3 with one digit wanted and none entered, six wires in positions 1 to 6. deaf sees colours and tells me the wires are purple white blue green red orange. you are the only one holding the manual, so please read out the procedure for each module, speaking to me since I am the hands: what one digit goes into the keypad, what the green light and the strip segments require, and which wires if any must be cut and in what order. also please pass my reports to deaf with hand signs, since my voice never reaches them. I will not touch anything until I hear your instructions.
Deaf says: Blind, your thumbs-up reached me — well done. Orders from Mute, spoken through me: the manual wants three wires cut — position one, position three, position six. I number wire positions one to six from my left as I face the bomb. Before you cut anything, fix our reference. Feel the row of six wires and say aloud, for Mute: first, whether any wires differ by touch, thickness or texture; second, which end of the row sits nearest which part — the glass display, the four-key keypad, the small light, or the three-segment strip; third, whether you feel any engraved digits near the wire bases. If, and only if, you find a sure way to know which physical wire is my number one, cut one, then three, then six, reporting aloud after each. If you cannot be sure, cut nothing yet — one wrong wire kills all three of us. Now answers for Mute, spoken for everyone: wire six is orange, confirmed. Wire five is red — not purple, not blue, not green. Full row, my left to right: one purple, two white, three blue, four green, five red, six orange — all six still intact. Two changes since my last report: the light was green and is now blue; the display was zero and now reads six — if that is a timer, Mute, tell me what the manual says and we work fast. Questions for Mute: does the manual explain the display number, and the keypad? The keypad wants one digit from keys eight, one, five, three. Sign me: wave then punch for keypad, wave then heart-hands for display.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🫶 🤙]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤚 🫲]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤙 🤜]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 👊]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 🫶]

A cold reading of Deaf's broadcast uncovers a life-threatening error: Deaf told Blind "cut one, then three, then **six**." My third order was 🙏✍🖖 — cut wire **4** (split fingers = 4 in Deaf's own code), and wire 4 is green. Wire 6 is orange, which is not in my manual at all. If Deaf repeats that order once Blind feels confident of orientation, Blind cuts the wrong wire and we all die. Nobody has cut anything yet — Blind explicitly waits for instructions — so this is fixable, but only if my correction reaches Deaf this round.

My fix is to double-encode every cut with the wire's **colour**: 🫰 purple, 🫲 blue, 🫳 green. Deaf sees the bomb directly and already reported 1=purple, 3=blue, 4=green, 6=orange — so the colour makes the correction self-verifying: green can only be position 4 in Deaf's own visual frame, and any residual "6" dies on contact. I open with 👎 plus 🤙 (six) to flag that the error concerns wire 6, then re-send all three orders.

Deaf also asked whether the manual explains the display (now 0→6), the keypad, and the strip. It does not — my manual is exactly three wire cuts, nothing else. I answer each query in the 👋+topic format Deaf requested: no, no, no. The display change worries me (possibly a timer — I flag urgency in my ordering but the manual gives no meaning for it), and since the manual's only path to victory is the three cuts, I close by prompting Deaf to collect Blind's landmark report (which end of the wire row sits near which module), because Deaf's left and Blind's left may not match, and that shared reference is the last missing piece before any wire is cut.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "🤙"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "✍", "☝", "🫰"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "✍", "🤟", "🫲"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "✍", "🖖", "🫳"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👊", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫶", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🙌", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤙", "🖐", "🫶"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: blind to mute, answers to deaf's three questions, then a plan. please sign the parts marked FOR DEAF. ONE, wires by touch: all six are identical to my fingers, same thickness, same texture, evenly spaced, and there are no engravings near the wire bases. the only engravings anywhere on this bomb are the strip's three glyphs and the keypad's four digits. so touch alone cannot tell me which wire is deaf's number one. TWO, layout: my touch cannot give a trustworthy left-right map of the face, but I do have my own left and right by body, and I face the same face you and deaf do, the face holding display, light, strip, keypad and wires, so my left should equal deaf's left. I want one check before any blade touches a wire, because a mirrored count kills us. THREE, FOR DEAF, please sign: from your left, read out the keypad digit sequence. if your left-to-right reading is 8, 1, 5, 3 then my left is your left, anchor confirmed; if it is 3, 5, 1, 8, I mirror every position. FOUR, my plan once confirmed: I count wires from my left, wire one is first, and I cut one, then three, then six, in that order, all in one turn, since I cannot pause mid-turn for confirmation. deaf, watch the display and light as I cut. FIVE, for mute alone: the display moved from zero to six and the light from green to blue. if that display is a timer we are spending it right now, so please answer this round: what digit goes into the keypad, what the light colours demand, what the strip glyphs demand, and what the manual says the display number means. send your answers through deaf's voice, that is my only ear.
Deaf says: Blind, Mute — hear me. Blind first: do not cut anything yet. The next thing I want from you is not a cut, it is a report, spoken aloud for Mute to relay. One wrong wire kills all three of us, so we spend one round on certainty.
Deaf says: Mute, I read your orders as three cuts, and I act on your colour words: cut the purple wire, which on my board is position one; cut the blue wire, position three; cut the green wire, position four. Your first two numbers and colours agree with my eyes exactly. Wire six is orange and none of your orders mentions orange, so I believe my earlier reading of your third number as six was my mistake, not yours. Confirm for me next turn: if the cuts are exactly purple one, blue three, green four, sign one thumbs-up. If the manual wants any different wire — including position six — sign thumbs-down and then the number and colour you want. Also, if time is critical, sign two thumbs-down together.
Deaf says: Answers to all your repeated questions, Mute. The display now reads nine; its history is zero, then six, now nine — it is rising, so treat it as a timer. I have never seen sixty-five or any two-digit value. The light is still blue. The strip is still three segments, all green. Wire six is orange, confirmed again. Wire five is red, and no cut order you sent mentions red either. The keypad still wants exactly one digit and shows nothing entered; the keys in order are engraved eight, one, five, three. If the manual derives that digit from the display, light or strip, you now hold current values: display nine, light blue, strip green green green. When you know the digit, sign: wave, then the punch for keypad, then the digit.
Deaf says: Blind, your thumbs-up reached me, good. Do this now and speak it clearly for Mute: first, find the keypad by touch and read me its four engraved digits in the order you feel them from one end to the other, and say which end of the wire row that end is nearest. That fixes our shared left and right: if your digits from that end read eight, one, five, three, then that end is my position-one side, and wires count from there. Second, describe each of the six wires by feel, in a row, thickness or texture, so we can check the count. Third, tell us anything you feel on the display glass or anywhere else that seems marked. Then hold and wait. When Mute confirms my colour mapping, I will give the go order: you will cut position one, then position three, then position four, one at a time, saying each number aloud before you cut and waiting after each wire.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Reading the board: Deaf has fully absorbed my colour-coded orders and publicly retracted the "six" misreading — the cuts are agreed as purple 1, blue 3, green 4, which matches my manual exactly. Deaf asked for a single thumbs-up to lock that in; that is my first and most important send, because Deaf has promised the go order the moment I confirm. I follow it immediately with the three executable orders again, colours attached, so the confirmation and the order set sit side by side in one unambiguous package.

On urgency: the display has gone 0 → 6 → 9, rising every round. My manual says nothing about any display, so I cannot decode it — but a changing number on an armed bomb is a timer until proven otherwise, and my manual offers exactly one path to survival. So I send the agreed two-thumbs-down urgency signal: stop deliberating, execute.

On the keypad, display, light and strip: Deaf still hopes the manual derives a keypad digit from those values. It does not. My manual is three wire cuts and literally nothing else — the keypad "wanted digit" and the strip glyphs are bait, and a wrong press likely kills us. I answer each of Deaf's topic queries in the exact wave-plus-topic format Deaf requested, each with a thumbs-down: no digit, no display meaning, no strip instruction. I would rather repeat this than have anyone improvise a keypress to "help."

The geometry is working: Blind's voice reaches only me, my hands reach only Deaf, Deaf's voice reaches Blind — and Deaf has already spoken the keypad digits and left-numbering aloud, so Blind's anchor check needs no relay from me. Once Blind reports the digit order, Deaf can verify the reference and give the go in the same round. My job this round is to remove every reason for delay.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "✍", "☝", "🫰"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "✍", "🤟", "🫲"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "✍", "🖖", "🫳"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👊", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫶", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🙌", "👎"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: blind to mute, full tactile report as deaf requested, numbered for signing to deaf. ONE, keypad anchor: the keypad is four keys in a row. traversing it from one end, the digits under my fingers read eight, one, five, three. the end I started from, the eight end, is the same end of the face that wire position one sits on — the eight key and wire one are nearest each other. so sign to deaf: read the keypad from your left. if you read eight, one, five, three, our numbering matches and no mirroring is needed. if you read three, five, one, eight, we are mirrored and I will flip every position number. TWO, wires by feel, counted from the wire-one end: one, smooth, round, medium thickness. two, identical. three, identical. four, identical. five, identical. six, identical. all six same thickness, same insulation, evenly spaced, no tags, no texture differences, no engravings at the bases. the count is a clean six. THREE, display and the rest: the display glass is smooth with nothing raised or engraved on it. the light is a small smooth dome, unmarked. the only markings anywhere on this bomb are the strip's three raised glyphs, flower then two crescents, and the keypad's four digits. FOUR, I am holding, no cuts, exactly as deaf ordered. FIVE, resolve the cut list explicitly, positions only, never colour words, since colours are nothing to my fingers: the relay I heard in round three said cuts at one, three, six, and deaf now believes it was one, three, four. sign to deaf a thumbs-up if the manual's cuts are exactly position one, position three, position four; if any position differs, thumbs-down and the correct positions. SIX, still owed from the manual: what one digit goes into the keypad and whether it is entered before or after the cuts; what the light's colours demand, it went green then blue; what the strip's glyphs demand; and what the rising display, zero then six then nine, means. SEVEN, once deaf confirms the anchor and you confirm the three positions, I will follow deaf's go order: one cut at a time, position number spoken before each, unless you signal time-critical, and then I cut all three in a single turn.
Deaf says: Blind, good — your thumbs-up and open hand reached me. Here is where we stand. Mute has confirmed the manual's targets: cut the purple wire, then the blue wire, then the green wire — on my board those are positions one, three, and four. The white, red, and orange wires stay untouched. Before any cut we must anchor the positions by touch, and only you can do that. Do this now, and say every part aloud for Mute: first, find the keypad, four keys with engraved digits; read the engravings by touch starting from the end nearest the wire row, and say the four digits in the order you feel them. Second, run your fingers along the row of six wires and say whether any two differ in thickness, texture, or covering. Third, say what sits nearest each end of the wire row — the keypad, the display glass, the small light, or the three-part strip. Fourth, if the display glass or anything else carries raised or engraved marks, describe them. Then touch nothing else and wait. Next round I will speak the anchor and the go order. When you hear the word GO, you will cut one wire at a time, saying the position number aloud before each cut and pausing after it: position one, then position three, then position four. If anything you feel contradicts my description, cut nothing and say so instead.
Deaf says: Mute, I read your signs. The thumbs-up confirms the mapping — purple one, blue three, green four — locked in, and the repeated cut orders match it, so we agree. Two thumbs-down together: time is critical, understood, we compress every round we safely can. Your three questions, answered: keypad unchanged — wants exactly one digit, nothing entered, keys read eight, one, five, three in position order. Display reads nine and did NOT rise this round — history zero, six, nine, nine — so it may not be a simple counting timer; if the manual explains the display, sign me what it says. Strip still green, green, green. Light still blue. All six wires intact. I need two things from you next round. First: Blind will speak his touch findings this round — relay them word for word with the phone-hand prefix: the four keypad digits he feels from the wire-near end, any texture differences between wires, what sits near each end of the row, any raised marks. Second: if the manual derives the keypad digit from the display, light, or strip, you already hold every current value — display nine, light blue, strip three greens — so compute it now and sign it as wave, punch, then the digit. If there is a time limit, or the display number carries meaning, sign wave, heart-hands, then the fact.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 🫶]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 👊]

The anchor is now verifiable from data only I hold — I hear both voices, and the two readings match: Deaf reads the keypad 8, 1, 5, 3 from his left; Blind reads 8, 1, 5, 3 by touch from the end nearest wire one. By Deaf's own stated rule, that fixes Blind's wire-one end as Deaf's left — no mirroring. I am the only monkey who can perform this cross-check, so relaying it is my critical job this round: phone-hand prefix, keypad topic, the four digits in Deaf's number code, then a thumbs-up asserting the match. Deaf has already promised to speak the anchor and the GO order next round; my confirmation unblocks that path.

I also relay the rest of Blind's tactile report as requested: wires identical by feel, nothing raised on the display or light — no hidden tactile traps.

On Deaf's second request — "compute the keypad digit" — there is nothing to compute, and I must kill this question loop decisively: my manual contains the three cuts and nothing else. No digit, no display meaning, no strip requirement, no light requirement. I restate the manual's complete contents (three cuts: purple, blue, green) immediately beside the topic-by-topic negations, so "that is everything" is unmistakable and nobody improvises a keypress on a bait module.

Finally, I do not re-trigger the time-critical signal: the display stalled at 9 (0, 6, 9, 9), so there is no evidence of a fast fuse, and Deaf's pause-after-each-cut protocol lets him watch the light and display react — safer than a blind triple cut, and barely slower.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤳", "🤜", "🤞", "☝", "🖐", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤳", "🖐", "🤲"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤳", "🫶", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤳", "🤚", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👏", "👏", "👏", "🙏", "✍", "🫰", "🫲", "🫳"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👊", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫶", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🙌", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤚", "👎"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
